relations.myth: Ino becomes Leucothea and is identified as Roman Matuta
relations.note: The deified Ino-Leucothea is identified with Mater Matuta.
In the transferred Greek genealogy, Ino-Matuta is Cadmus' daughter.
In the transferred Greek genealogy, Ino-Matuta is Harmonia's daughter.
Ino is the wife of Athamas in the inherited Greek genealogy.
Ino is Learchus' mother in the inherited Greek genealogy.
Ino-Leucothea is mother of Melicertes-Palaemon, identified at Rome as Portunus.

relations.myth: Mother and child leap into the sea and become divine
relations.note: Ino carries Melicertes into the sea; they become Leucothea and Palaemon.
Ino is Semele's sister in the transferred Greek genealogy.

relations.myth: Ino nurses her sister Semele's divine child
relations.note: Ino acts as maternal aunt and foster-mother to Dionysus.

relations.myth: Juno persecutes Ino for fostering Bacchus
relations.note: Juno's anger drives Athamas and Ino into madness and familial catastrophe.

relations.myth: Venus petitions Neptune to save Ino and Melicertes
relations.note: Venus intercedes with Neptune for her endangered divine relatives.

relations.myth: Neptune grants divinity to Ino and Melicertes
relations.note: At Venus' request, Neptune removes Ino's mortality and grants divine majesty.

relations.myth: Ino and Melicertes receive maritime apotheosis
relations.note: Amphitrite participates with Neptune in the mother and child's apotheosis.

relations.myth: Leucothea saves Odysseus from drowning with her veil
relations.note: Ino-Leucothea gives Odysseus her veil and directs his escape from the sea.
Ino's Italian arrival produces a hostile encounter near Hercules' altar before reconciliation.

relations.myth: Maenads threaten Leucothea near the Ara Maxima
relations.note: Maenads attack or threaten Leucothea during her arrival in Latium.

relations.myth: Carmenta foretells Leucothea's Roman name and cult
relations.note: Carmenta recognizes Leucothea and prophesies that Romans will call her Matuta.

relations.myth: Leucothea arrives in the future Roman landscape
relations.note: The Tiber god receives or marks Leucothea's arrival in Latium.
Their adjacent Roman temples shared a dedication date, burned together, and were rebuilt together.
Matuta performs the role of rosy dawn and is often equated with Aurora.
The Etruscan dawn goddess entered a reconstructed interpretive network linking Matuta and Leucothea.
The Greek dawn goddess is used as a comparative equivalent of dawn-associated Matuta.
Interpretive traditions connect their overlapping associations with birth and successful passage into life.
Greek interpretation at Pyrgi links Eileithyia with the Matuta-Leucothea cultic field.
A dedication to Mars was reused within Mater Matuta's later Satricum sanctuary.
